sources.entry: FlareSolverr | Proxy server to bypass Cloudflare protection for indexers

summary.one_liner: FlareSolverr is a proxy server that uses a headless Chrome browser to solve Cloudflare and DDoS-GUARD challenges and returns the HTML and cookies to other HTTP clients.
summary.what_it_does: It runs an idle HTTP proxy server that accepts JSON commands (request.get, request.post, sessions.create, sessions.list, sessions.destroy). On each request it launches a Chrome browser via Selenium and undetected-chromedriver, opens the URL, and waits until the Cloudflare challenge is solved or a timeout (maxTimeout, default 60 seconds) is reached. It then returns the page HTML, cookies, and user agent so other HTTP clients can reuse them. Persistent browser sessions can keep cookies across requests, with optional per-session proxies, TTL rotation, and cookie injection. Extra options include screenshots, disabling media loading, waiting before returning, and a Turnstile tab-count parameter. It also exposes an optional Prometheus exporter and is configured through environment variables such as LOG_LEVEL, PROXY_URL, TZ, and LANG.
use_cases: get cookies to use with other HTTP clients past a Cloudflare challenge
proxy requests for indexers blocked by Cloudflare
reuse a browser session across many requests
how_to_run: docker compose up -d (using the repository's docker-compose.yml)
pip install -r requirements.txt (from source, Python 3.11, Chrome or Chromium, Xvfb on Linux)
notable: Accepts simple JSON POST commands, so any HTTP client can use it without a browser
Persistent sessions with optional TTL rotation and per-session proxies
Precompiled binaries, Docker images for x86, x86-64, ARM32 and ARM64, and a systemd unit example
Optional screenshot capture and tmpfs /tmp guidance to reduce disk wear
Prometheus metrics for request counts and durations
caveats: Each request launches a full browser, which uses a lot of memory; running many requests at once needs substantial RAM
The README states that none of the captcha solvers currently work
Precompiled binaries are only for x64, and source install is also x64-only per the README; use Docker for other architectures
The README warns not to expose it to the internet because it can be abused
keywords: cookie and user agent for http clients
